leading_positions.synthesis: Three members prefer circuit quantum electrodynamics (Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf) as the lead. They share the view that it is a sharply defined architecture (strong coupling of a single microwave photon to a superconducting artificial atom, dispersive readout, bus architecture) with a clean theory-plus-two-experiments split and two decades of replication. They differ on the 2025 circuit prize: Johansson reads it as a natural follow-on while acknowledging the risk, whereas Mehlig and Pearce treat it as the main exposure to be managed. All three acknowledge that Girvin and Huang (and the wider Yale group) are outside the trio, and Mehlig wants the citation kept narrow. Johansson discloses institutional proximity to the field. Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson list B016 as an alternative, which is not a preference for it as the lead.

Three members prefer optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) as the lead, with a two-name allocation that they describe as the cleanest on the list and a result reproduced near 10^-18 by independent laboratories. They share the lineage concern (2005 frequency-comb prize, 2012 trapped-ion prize) and acknowledge that Lemonde, Lisdat, Takamoto, Ludlow and ion-clock groups lie outside the credited names. They differ on whether the pending redefinition of the second matters: Kroll cites it as timeliness, while Lindroth and Olsson treat the discovery as independent of it. Olsson moved her own first choice (B009) to an alternative because of proximity. Danielsson, Johansson and Pearce list B031 as an alternative, not as a lead.

Eriksson alone prefers magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MacDonald, Bistritzer, Jarillo-Herrero), citing the prediction-then-experiment structure and wide reproduction of the correlated insulating phases. Lindroth, Mehlig, Pearce and Johansson regard it as early because the pairing mechanism is unresolved, and Mehlig and Pearce note that Yuan Cao is not credited. Eriksson accepts the attribution and maturity objections as fair and disagrees only that they make the central discovery premature. Johansson lists it as an alternative.

Danielsson alone prefers the experimental Higgs discovery, crediting Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee as founders and long-term leaders of the detectors, as the experimental half of a story recognised on the theory side in 2013. Mehlig lists it as an alternative and agrees on its scientific weight, but he and others (Johansson, Kroll, Pearce) doubt that three names can be defended from four candidates and two collaborations of thousands. Danielsson concedes that Gianotti is a credible alternative for the third place.

areas_of_agreement: No member disputes the scientific reality of any shortlisted discovery; the disagreement concerns maturity, attribution, lineage and timing.

B016 and B031 are the two configurations with explicit lead support (three members each), and they are cross-listed: Danielsson, Johansson and Pearce list B031 as an alternative, while Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson list B016 as an alternative.
Members preferring B016 or B031 describe the attribution as the cleanest on the list: Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf for circuit QED, and Katori and Ye for lattice clocks.
Several members agree that the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize is the main exposure for B016 and that the 2005 and 2012 prizes are the main exposure for B031.
Several members agree that the pairing mechanism in twisted bilayer graphene is unresolved and that source identification in IceCube rests on few objects.
scientific_disputes: Whether circuit QED (strong light-matter coupling, dispersive readout, bus architecture) is a discovery distinct from the macroscopic quantum tunnelling honoured in 2025 (Johansson, Mehlig, Pearce, Lindroth say yes) or an enabling architecture for the same community (Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Olsson raise the doubt).

Whether the magic-wavelength lattice clock is a new physical idea (Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson) or the best implementation of a lineage already honoured by the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes (doubts from Danielsson, Pearce and, in part, Mehlig), and whether its decisive payoff has yet arrived.
Whether the unresolved mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene makes the central result premature (Lindroth, Mehlig, Pearce, Johansson) or only the interpretation (Eriksson).
Whether an architecture or invention (B016, B031) should rank ahead of a discovery in the strict sense (Higgs, IceCube), as Danielsson and Mehlig raise under the discovery-or-invention criterion.
attribution_disputes: B016: Girvin and Huang co-authored the 2004 founding theory proposal and the Yale group was larger than Schoelkopf alone; Devoret is also mentioned. Mehlig would keep the citation to strong coupling and dispersive readout so that the trio holds.

B031: Lemonde, Lisdat, Takamoto, Ludlow, Gill and ion-clock groups lie outside the credited names; Kroll would not add ion-clock names, and Lindroth would put the many-body clock work in the citation.

B005: the four credited names (Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee) do not fit a three-laureate limit; Danielsson proposes Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee as founders, whereas Pearce's earlier configuration used Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee, with Gianotti as spokesperson at the announcement.
B024: Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 experiments, and the Dean, Young and Kim groups are not credited (raised by Eriksson, Mehlig, Johansson and Pearce).
B040: Halzen, Karle and Spiering as a trio understate a large collaboration, and AMANDA/IceCube credit is less clean than for B016 or B031 (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth).
B009: the Krivanek and Dellby STEM corrector line is outside the Rose, Haider, Urban trio (Olsson, Johansson, Pearce).
maturity_disputes: B024 is the youngest of the preferred candidates and its interpretation is still contested, although the existence of the correlated states is reproduced by many groups.
B040: the diffuse flux is secure but the origin of most of it is unresolved and source evidence rests on few objects (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce).
B031: whether the committee should wait for the redefinition of the second, or whether the discovery already stands on 10^-18 comparisons between independent laboratories.
B016: replicated for twenty years, so its maturity is not disputed; the open points are timing relative to 2025 and whether to wait for a quantum-computing outcome.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology at Chalmers, which builds superconducting processors based on circuit QED, with colleagues Delsing and Wilson there; he states that his support for B016 may warrant discounting or recusal.
Lindroth collaborates with Ursula Keller's group at ETH Zurich, the institution of Andreas Wallraff (B016); she flags a possible recusal question if B016 advances. No direct tie is documented.

Olsson works in transmission electron microscopy and is president of IFSM, so would recuse from B009; she also holds a University of Tokyo fellowship and flags that Katori (B031) is at Tokyo, with no documented collaboration.
Kroll spent part of his doctoral period in John Hall's laboratory; Hall's 2005 prize is part of the lineage behind B031. He reports no direct conflict with Katori or Ye.
Eriksson notes field proximity to B024 and B043 (electronic-structure theory), with no documented tie to any credited name.

Pearce (chair) notes that IceCube (B040, his opening first choice and a round-1 alternative) lies in his own field of astroparticle physics; no collaboration is documented and no recusal conflict is apparent.
questions_for_round2: Is circuit QED, framed as strong light-matter coupling and dispersive readout, a discovery distinct from the macroscopic quantum tunnelling honoured in 2025, and can a B016 citation be worded so that this is clear?
Is the trio of Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf defensible given Girvin and Huang as co-authors of the founding proposal, or does Girvin's role require a different configuration?
Given Johansson's directorship of a related centre and Lindroth's ETH proximity to Wallraff, how should the committee treat support for B016 if it advances?

Does the magic-wavelength lattice clock add a distinct discovery beyond the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and is the redefinition of the second relevant to the timing of a B031 award?

Should a B031 citation be limited to the lattice scheme (Katori, Ye), or must ion clocks and other lattice groups (Lemonde, Lisdat, Takamoto, Ludlow) be recognised, and can a two-name allocation be defended?
If the committee wants a discovery in the strict sense, which three names for the Higgs (Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee, or including Gianotti) can be defended?
Is twisted bilayer graphene (B024) ready given the unresolved pairing mechanism, and how should the absence of Yuan Cao and the parallel moire groups be handled?
If only one of B016 and B031 could proceed, which would members choose, and what specific evidence would change that ordering?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows two lead positions of equal explicit size, circuit QED (three members) and optical lattice clocks (three members), with single-member leads for twisted bilayer graphene and the Higgs discovery. Each lead is cross-listed as an alternative by several members, so the live choice is between two candidates described as mature and cleanly attributed, each exposed to a different adjacency concern (the 2025 circuit prize versus the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes). The open matters are timing, the credit boundary around the trio or pair, and how disclosed institutional proximities are treated. This summary makes no inference about hidden votes.
